requirement:
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
rationale:
I found no gaps. I did not read the rest of `src/outline/rust.rs` (`attaches`, `is_comment` and similar); the judgment rests on the cited items, the tests and the book text.

**Obligations, code and tests**

1. **Segments describing syntactic ancestry within the file** (`fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, `mod[local]/fn[run]`).
   - Code: the `KINDS` table and `PROFILE` in `src/outline/rust.rs` (lines 131–172) map grammar kinds to outline kinds and name rules. Descendants nest under the nearest outline ancestor.
   - Tests: `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` (`src/outline/tests.rs:35`) and `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` (`:657`) assert `mod[local]/fn[run]`, `fn[outer]/fn[inner]`, `trait[Trait]/fn[read]` and `extern[C]/fn[puts]`. They also assert that duplicates become `fn[repeated]#1` and `#2`.
2. **MUST NOT resolve Rust modules across files.**
   - Code: `KINDS` maps `mod_item` as an ordinary named node, and the table never touches other files. `mod external;` becomes just `mod[external]`.
   - Test: the two tests above assert `mod[external]`.
3. **Items that MUST be outline nodes** (functions, methods, structs, enums, unions, traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, extern blocks).
   - Code: every one of these has a `KindRule` in `KINDS`: `function_item`, `function_signature_item`, `struct_item`, `enum_item`, `union_item`, `trait_item`, `impl_item`, `mod_item`, `macro_definition`, item-position `macro_invocation`, `const_item`, `static_item`, `type_item`, `associated_type` and `foreign_mod_item`.
   - Tests: `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` asserts `fn`, `struct`, `enum[E]`, `union[U]`, `trait`, `impl`, `mod`, `macro[make]`, `const[C]`, `static[S]`, `type[Alias]`, `extern[C]`, `extern[Rust]`, `extern-crate[core]` and the associated `type[Item]`. Methods are covered as `impl[Thing]/fn[run]`.
4. **Impl segments named by syntactic self type and optional trait path.**
   - Code: `impl_name` (`rust.rs:7`) uses the `type` field plus the `trait` field when present.
   - Tests: `impl[Thing]`, `impl[Thing/Trait]`, `impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]` (an array self type, percent-encoded), and `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]` in `item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not` (`:932`).
5. **`use` declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous.**
   - Code: `use_declaration` and item-position `macro_invocation` use `NameRule::Anonymous`. The helpers `item_macro` and `in_item_list` (`rust.rs:50`, `:57`) restrict macro nodes to item position. `extern_name` (`rust.rs:22`) falls back to `Rust` when an extern block has no ABI string.
   - Tests: `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` asserts `use@…` selectors that differ from each other. `item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not` asserts `macro@<12 hex>` for item macros, and that expression macros inside function bodies are not nodes. `extern[Rust]` is asserted in the first test.
6. **Selector spelling MUST be documented.**
   - `md/reference.md` has a "Rust items" section. It gives `mod[local]/fn[run]`, `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]`, the `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]` example, anonymous `use@…` and item-position macros, and says modules are never resolved across files.
   - The "Selectors" section covers the `kind[name]` and `kind@hash` forms, `#N` and percent-encoding. The "Outline profiles" table lists every Rust kind and its naming rule.

**Marking:** the `{impl}` and `{test}` references are present on the relevant items. I found no other unmarked implementing or testing code.

**Unspecified behavior:** the extra `extern-crate` kind and the `Rust` default for extern blocks without an ABI string are documented in the profile table and fall within "other items".

text: :::{req} rust_item_selectors
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
:::{req} outlines
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension compared
case-insensitively. A source with any syntax error MUST fail to parse, reporting
the line of its first error. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline; other
nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline descendants appear under the
nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
:::{definition} definition_selection
:phrase: definition selection
A full requirement or example name, or a definition glob, identifying the
requirements and named examples it matches under
{cite}`requirements.references.definition_globs`. A name without `*` selects
exactly that definition.
